label: Modal spine stage one: rivals of five premises and their survival models
summary: Run goal: every open premise of the modal spine to God's existence gets a recorded rival with a replacement account and one verified test (docs/notes/modal-spine.md, rival table). This attempt covers the five stage-one premises that had no rival: actual reflexivity, the Euclidean frame, presence-to-existence, the possible beginning and the causal opportunity. Each rival is a positive position typed on the premise's carrier: a serial frame not reflexive at the selected world (accessibility read as what lies ahead or what would be ideal); a reflexive non-Euclidean frame (relative, non-transitive possibility); a presentist gap (existence is presence now and something earlier has ceased); eternal contingency (contingent things and no possible beginning); brute beginnings only. All five survive: SpineRivalsStageOne.controls gives, for each, an interpretation in which the rival holds with the other premises of the consuming theorem and the conclusion fails. The brute-beginnings group reuses the existing bruteOnly scenario and its lemmas. Findings: the presentist model shows the temporal arrival depends on reading world-relative existence as existence at some time; under presentism an earlier non-contingent occupant can have ceased, so the conclusion would need a persistence premise. The reflexivity rival does not deny that what is actual is possible; it changes the meaning of accessibility, which is why actual reflexivity is listed as a floor candidate. No rival is refuted and no premise is established.
blocker: No conditional exclusion was sought for these five rivals. Next discriminators: the existing modal correspondence results for the non-Euclidean rival, and a persistence premise for the presentist rival.
